business_problem: Banco do Brasil needed much faster access to current mainframe data for tens of thousands of reporting dashboards and core processes such as loan handling, CRM, budgeting, and loss monitoring, but consolidated information generation still took more than 24 hours and relied on expensive multi-platform analytics estates.
solution_summary: IBM implemented Db2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS so Banco do Brasil could run complex analytics directly against current mainframe data without waiting for slow overnight consolidation. The accelerator became the backbone for more than 70,000 branch dashboards and numerous departmental reporting workloads, including Internal Controls, productivity tracking, and customer-relationship analysis. The bank also consolidated product-level marts for savings, checking, credit cards, and insurance into a single warehouse view, which improved cost transparency and created a 360-degree customer perspective for CRM and cross-sell analysis. Underneath, the analytics estate runs across six IBM LinuxONE machines with more than 1,200 IFLs supporting 14 accelerators and more than a petabyte of data, split across two geographically separate data centers for high availability and disaster recovery. This architecture let the bank move loan information turnaround from 24 hours to minutes while supporting a quarter of a million complex queries and 138 terabytes of daily workload at enterprise scale.
products_used: IBM Db2 Analytics Accelerator for z/OS

data_flow: Current mainframe banking data is queried through Db2 Analytics Accelerator, consolidated into branch dashboards and departmental reporting, and then reused by loan processing, CRM, budget planning, sales productivity tracking, and enterprise financial analysis without moving the bank onto separate reporting platforms.
business_outcome: Banco do Brasil gave thousands of employees near-real-time access to mainframe analytics, improved customer and branch decision-making, retired separate reporting platforms, and established a highly competitive data-driven operating model.
